q1.prompt: A recursive solution must terminate. What must every recursive function include?

choices.label: A base case that returns without calling itself, plus a strictly smaller subproblem
Only a recursive call — the runtime will stop somehow

wrong_nobase.prompt: Without a base case the stack grows forever.
wrong_nobase.explanation: Recursion needs a base case, a move to a smaller subproblem, and an account of stack space. Omitting the base case never terminates.

q2.prompt: Which recursive implementation needs a different plan?

choices.label: Without a base case, when the step does not shrink, or when O(depth) stack on skewed input is ignored
Recursion is always safer than an explicit loop

wrong_refuse.explanation: Avoid recursion without a base case. Avoid a recursive step that does not shrink the problem. Avoid ignoring O(depth) stack space on skewed inputs.

success.prompt: You required base cases and avoided non-shrinking or stack-blind recursion.
